speaker: Ali Khamenei (Supreme Leader)
what: In a speech a day after the Iraq invasion began: 'We don't want a nuclear bomb. We are even opposed to having chemical weapons.'
notes: As quoted (from farsi.khamenei.ir, speech id 3167) by Khosro Sayeh Isfahani, Atlantic Council, 9 May 2024. Date inferred from 'the day after' the 20 March invasion. Not called a fatwa.

speaker: Hassan Rohani (Secretary, Supreme National Security Council)
what: Told students in Shahrud that the Leader regards efforts to obtain nuclear weapons as religiously illegal.
notes: IRNA dispatch via GlobalSecurity.org. Usually cited as the first public reference to the ruling.

speaker: Iranian delegation to the IAEA Board of Governors
what: Statement at the emergency Board meeting: the Leader has issued a fatwa that 'the production, stockpiling, and use of nuclear weapons are forbidden under Islam' and Iran 'shall never acquire these weapons'.
notes: IRNA text dated 10 Aug 2005 (read 'Tuesday evening', 9 Aug), reproduced by Juan Cole. This is the version with 'production' and 'stockpiling'; Khamenei's own later wording mostly concerns use.

speaker: Ali Khamenei (Supreme Leader)
what: Message to the Tehran disarmament conference: 'we consider the use of such weapons as haram' and it is everyone's duty to protect humanity from them.
notes: IRNA via GlobalSecurity.org. The Leader's Farsi website later filed this passage in its fatwa section ('Prohibition of weapons of mass destruction'). Registered at the UN as A/64/752-S/2010/203.

speaker: Ali Khamenei (Supreme Leader)
what: To nuclear officials and scientists: Iran 'has never pursued and will never pursue nuclear weapons'; possessing them is a great sin.
notes: RFE/RL via GlobalSecurity.org. Translations differ ('great', 'big', 'grave' sin).

speaker: Juan Cole (University of Michigan, blog Informed Comment)
what: Rebuttal of MEMRI: 'Yes, MEMRI, there is a fatwa', citing the 2005 IAEA statement and other references.
notes: Part of the 2012 debate over whether a fatwa exists; a defence of its existence.

speaker: MEMRI (Middle East Media Research Institute)
what: A newly published compilation of 493 of Khamenei's 'newest' fatwas did not include any fatwa on nuclear weapons; MEMRI calls the fatwa 'nonexistent'.
notes: Special Dispatch No. 5406. Advocacy-leaning institute; MEMRI repeats the claim in 2025 and February 2026 reports.

speaker: Gareth Porter (journalist), in Foreign Policy
what: Argues the ruling dates from a mid-1990s letter never made public and reflects a sincere aversion rooted in the Iran-Iraq war.
notes: A defence of the fatwa's standing, citing Seyed Hossein Mousavian's recollection of the letter.

speaker: Ali Khamenei (Supreme Leader)
what: To panegyrists: 'Both shar'i and aqli fatwas dictate that we do not pursue them' and a nuclear weapon is 'a source of trouble for a country like ours'.
notes: Leader's English website (archived copy).

speaker: Ali Khamenei (Supreme Leader)
what: 'Both building and stockpiling it is wrong, as using it is haram'; Iran could have built a bomb but declared it forbidden.
notes: Reuters copy via Israel Hayom; one of the few statements extending the ban explicitly to building and stockpiling.

speaker: Mahmoud Alavi (Intelligence Minister)
what: The fatwa forbids nuclear weapons, but 'a cornered cat may behave differently'; if Iran were pushed that way, it would not be Iran's fault.
notes: Reuters, 9 February 2021 (state TV interview).

speaker: Ali Khamenei (Supreme Leader)
what: Said the West could not stop Iran building nuclear arms if it chose to; it was not doing so because of its beliefs.
notes: Reuters, 11 June 2023 (link via Atlantic Council).

speaker: Ahmad Haghtalab (IRGC commander for nuclear security)
what: Warned that Israeli threats against nuclear sites could lead to a 'revision of Islamic Republic's nuclear policies and doctrine'.
notes: Iran International. On 22 April the foreign ministry (Kanaani) said nuclear weapons 'have no place' in Iran's defence doctrine (Mehr, via Atlantic Council).

speaker: Kamal Kharrazi (adviser to the Supreme Leader)
what: 'We have no decision to build a nuclear bomb', but if Iran's existence were threatened it would have 'no choice but to change our military doctrine'.
notes: Al Jazeera Mubasher interview.

speaker: Khosro Sayeh Isfahani, Atlantic Council IranSource
what: Argues no written fatwa exists: of 85 quotes on Khamenei's site 'haram' appears three times, always about use, never production or stockpiling.
notes: Think-tank analysis.

speaker: 39 members of parliament
what: Letter to the Supreme National Security Council calling for a 'revision of Iran's nuclear doctrine' and asking Khamenei to reconsider the fatwa.
notes: Dawn (AFP), October 2024.

speaker: Kamal Kharrazi (adviser to the Supreme Leader)
what: Iran has the technical capability to make weapons and only the religious decree prevents it; 'If the survival of Iran comes under serious threat, we reserve the right to reconsider'.
notes: Iran International; first comments after Israel's 26 Oct 2024 strikes.

speaker: IRGC commanders (anonymous, reported)
what: Senior commanders were reported to have urged Khamenei to revoke the fatwa against nuclear weapons.
notes: The Telegraph; anonymous sourcing, not confirmed by Iran.

speaker: Ali Larijani (adviser to the Supreme Leader)
what: A US or Israeli attack would leave Iran 'no choice' but to move toward a nuclear weapon.
notes: State TV interview. Larijani later became SNSC secretary and was killed on 17 March 2026.

speaker: 71 members of parliament
what: Letter asking for a reassessment of defence doctrine, arguing that the fatwa concerns use and that possessing weapons for deterrence would not violate it.
notes: Iran International; the government did not comment.

speaker: Masoud Pezeshkian (President)
what: Said the Supreme Leader's fatwa prohibits weapons of mass destruction, so Tehran will 'categorically' not develop nuclear weapons.
notes: Two days before Ali Khamenei was killed.

speaker: Abbas Araghchi (Foreign Minister)
what: Asked about the new leader's position, said he did not know it; Iran's policy 'will not be different from our previous policy' but they must wait for his positions.
notes: Al Jazeera interview as reported by Ynet (March 2026; exact day not given, placed mid-month).

speaker: Islamic Republic of Iran (US-Iran memorandum)
what: 'The Islamic Republic of Iran reaffirms that it shall not procure or develop nuclear weapons.'
notes: Paragraph 8 of the memorandum; a treaty-style pledge, not a religious ruling. Mojtaba Khamenei endorsed the memorandum on 18 June (site's tracker), without mention of the fatwa.

speaker: Masoud Pezeshkian (President)
what: 'Developing nuclear weapons is haram'; even if some in Iran wanted one, religiously they may not pursue it.
notes: CBS News interview; he did not mention the fatwa by name or the new leader's view on it.

speaker: Ahmad Naderi (MP, parliamentary leadership)
what: 'From Mojtaba Khamenei's behavior, my understanding is that his fatwa will be different'; circumstances have changed since Iran was attacked.
notes: Speculation, not a statement by the Leader. MEF dates his remark (to Khabar Online) 18 Oct 2026.

speaker: Paydari Front (hardline party led by Saeed Jalili)
what: Called for Iran's withdrawal from the NPT.
notes: Middle East Forum, 4 Nov 2026, citing Donya-e-Eqtesad.

speaker: Mohammad-Javad Haj Ali-Akbari (interim Friday prayer leader, Tehran)
what: Called revising the doctrine and moving toward a weapon a 'national demand' and urged experts to put proposals to Mojtaba Khamenei for a final decision.
notes: The Telegraph via Yahoo, 2 Nov 2026. His claim of 70% public support is unsourced.

speaker: Mohsen Rezaei (Secretary, Supreme National Security Council)
what: No decision has been made to change the doctrine, but 'If war breaks out again, do we want to keep the same old doctrine?'
notes: Also said Iran's future in the NPT was uncertain, then walked it back (MEF, citing ISNA and Nournews).

speaker: Esmail Baghaei (Foreign Ministry spokesman)
what: Changing the doctrine is 'a real issue': 'The other side has assassinated the person who issued the fatwa banning the production and use of nuclear weapons.'
notes: The Telegraph via Yahoo, 2 Nov 2026. He also said Iran remains bound by the NPT.

speaker: Mojtaba Khamenei (Supreme Leader since March 2026)
what: No public statement found keeping, restating or changing his father's fatwa as of 8 November 2026 (his messages of 4 and 7 November threaten a wider war without mentioning nuclear weapons); hardliners expect his ruling 'will be different', and officials say any change rests with him.
notes: Searched Mar-Nov 2026 coverage (Ynet, Iran International 2 Nov, Telegraph 2 Nov, MEF 4 Nov): none attributes a nuclear statement to him. Tasnim reported he told commanders to respond 'without geographical limitations', with no order on weapons. Row dated to the day of this check (status as of 7 Nov 2026).
